title: Memory machines in Ada Lovelace’s meta-archive
abstract: Taking Ada Lovelace’s careful orchestration of her own funeral and interment as a point of departure, this article examines how her memory has been constructed, mediated, and mobilised across time. It introduces the concept of memory machines to trace the layered entanglements of material traces, emotional residues, and institutional practices through which women mathematicians are remembered. Focusing on Lovelace’s meta-archive—understood as a shifting field of documents, silences, and curatorial choices—the article explores how memory takes shape not only through what is preserved but through affective attachments and archival infrastructures. Memory machines provide a framework for mapping these operations without reducing them to narrative recovery or linear commemoration. In conclusion, the article reflects on the broader implications of this approach for the historiography of women in mathematics, suggesting new ways of engaging with archival remains as sites of encounter, interpretation, and imaginative reconstruction.
